checks.explanation: Well over 1,500 people were federally charged in connection with the January 6 Capitol riot, with hundreds convicted of felonies and many receiving prison sentences in the years that followed.

Trump was convicted of 34 felony counts in the New York hush-money case in 2024, but was sentenced to an 'unconditional discharge' in January 2025, meaning he faced no jail time, fine, or probation; he never actually went to jail.

sources.title: Trump sentenced to unconditional discharge in New York hush money case, avoiding jail

checks.explanation: The weeks following January 6 were indeed politically messy, including a second impeachment of Trump, intense public disputes over accountability and forgiveness, and significant overreach and backlash on multiple sides.

Decentralized platforms like Mastodon did gain a real user surge (notably around 2022-2023 amid Twitter's ownership change), but adoption stayed far below mainstream-competitor scale, and the claim that such platforms would be effectively unbannable proved only partly true, since app stores and hosting providers retained meaningful ability to restrict specific instances.

Trump faced federal January 6-related criminal charges (later dropped after his 2024 election win) and Rudy Giuliani faced disbarment and a massive defamation judgment plus Georgia RICO charges tied to his post-election conduct; both squarely faced the predicted civil/criminal exposure.
Parler itself relaunched, and other alternative platforms (Gettr, Truth Social, Rumble) emerged and grew to serve similar audiences after the January 2021 deplatforming wave.

Big Tech content-moderation and deplatforming actions did continue and expand through 2021-2022, but the trend later reversed in important ways, most notably Elon Musk's 2022 acquisition of Twitter/X, which significantly loosened moderation and reinstated many previously banned accounts, complicating the straightforward 'ever-expanding' narrative.
The House select committee to investigate the January 6 attack conducted extensive hearings in 2021-2022 and was widely and explicitly compared to the 9/11 Commission in scope and formality.

As of 2026, Meta (Facebook) has not been broken up; a federal judge ruled in Meta's favor in the FTC's monopolization case in November 2025, finding Meta does not currently hold a personal-social-networking monopoly, and the FTC's appeal of that ruling remains pending.

Within the 2-3 year window, significant Big Tech regulatory clarity did emerge: the EU's Digital Markets Act took effect in 2023 imposing major new obligations on large platforms, and the US DOJ won its landmark search-monopoly case against Google in August 2024, even though a full breakup did not occur.

Trump was anything but quiet in his final days in office: he was impeached a second time on January 13, 2021, continued public disputes over the election, and issued a large wave of pardons before leaving office.
